answers.text: Offer accepted, so send the offer letter and welcome email. Set up the Outlook calendar invites for the first-week meetings. Book the interviews and orientation slots. Put the new hire in the onboarding checklist sheet and tick off each item. Confirm the laptop and badge request. Send the benefits and leave FAQ link. Check the records are updated in the HR system before the start day.

design.read: From now on, each new hire is one row in a single tracker, and every step is dated from the start day for you. You no longer work out dates by hand or scan a checklist for what is late. The tracker shows the next date due in each row and marks it Due once that day has come, so you can see at a glance which of your new hires needs you today.

material.label: Your new hire tracker
items: Column A: New hire
Column B: Start day
Column C: Offer letter and welcome email
Column D: Calendar invites for first week
Column E: Interviews and orientation booked
Column F: Laptop and badge confirmed
Column G: Benefits and leave FAQ sent
Column H: HR system records checked
Column I: Next due
Column J: Status

material.label: Your next due formulas
items: I2: =IF(COUNT(C2:H2)=0,"All done",MIN(C2:H2))
J2: =IF(AND(I2<>"",ISNUMBER(I2),I2<=TODAY()),"Due","")

material.label: Your due date highlight
items: =AND(ISNUMBER(I2),I2<=TODAY())

steps.say: Set up the tracker with one row for each new hire, and date every step from the start day. Tally has written the columns and the day counts, which you can change to match how you work.
Add the Next due column and the Status column so each row shows its earliest step still to do.
Make the Next due dates stand out once the day has come.
When you get a new offer acceptance, add a row with the name and start day, then copy the date formulas down from the row above.
Each morning, open the tracker and work through the rows marked Due. When a step is finished, type done over its date.
Once a new hire shows All done, move that row to your archive sheet so the tracker holds only people still being onboarded.

design.tryOn: Your next two or three new hires, starting from their start days.
design.good: Every new hire has one row, each step has a date, and you see which rows are Due without checking a separate checklist.
design.approval: Check each start day and each date before you rely on it, and confirm the laptop, badge and HR system records yourself before the first day.

answers.text: Hi, I'm going on leave at the start of next month and I'm not sure if I need to change my health plan before it starts. Does coverage stop on the last day I work, and is there a deadline to add my new baby? Thanks, I need to submit before Friday.

design.read: From now on, colleagues enter their benefits enrollment questions themselves in one form, instead of writing to you one by one. Every request arrives with who it is from, what it is about, how urgent it is and when it is needed. You read them all in one place, so you stop sorting through email.

material.label: Your benefits enrollment form
items: Title: Benefits enrollment request

Your full name
Their own words

What is your request about?
Changing my health plan
Adding a family member
When my coverage starts or ends
Leave and benefits
Something else

How urgent is it?
I need an answer today
I need an answer this week
No rush

When do you need it by?
Their own words

Tell us a little more
Their own words

material.label: Your message with the link
items: Hi all, for any benefits enrollment question or change, please use this form instead of emailing me: [link]. It asks who you are, what it is about, how urgent it is and when you need it by. I will read every answer in one place and reply to you. Thanks, [your name]

material.label: Your benefits enrollment list
items: Open the form answers in Excel and leave that workbook as it is.
Read each row: name, request type, urgency, date needed and details.
On the form's results page, the count for each request type and urgency is already shown.

steps.say: Create the form. Tally has written the questions for you.
Send the form link to your colleagues using the message Tally wrote.
Each time you sit down to work on enrollment, open the results page to see how many requests there are for each type and how urgent they are.
Open the answers in Excel to read each person's request, who it is from and when they need it. Leave the workbook as it is.

Reply to each person, starting with the most urgent and earliest dates. When a round of enrollment is finished, start the next one by deleting the old answers in Forms once you have recorded what you need.

design.tryOn: The next benefits enrollment questions that reach you this week.
design.good: Colleagues send their requests through the form, and you see each one with who it is from, what it is about, how urgent it is and when it is needed, with no email sorting.
design.approval: Before you reply to anyone or change anything in a benefits record, check the person's details and the deadline yourself.
